descriptionChirho: The masculine noun saba designating a state of plenty, abundance, or satiety -- the condition of having more than enough, particularly of food and material provision. This term appears predominantly in the Joseph narrative describing Egypt's seven years of plenty (Gen 41:29-34, 41:47, 41:53) and in wisdom literature about the satiety of the rich (Eccl 5:12) and the fullness of the righteous (Prov 3:10). All three sense clusters convey the same core meaning of abundance/fullness in different syntactic environments: with article or standalone (6x), with conjunctive waw (1x), and bare noun (1x). Multilingual evidence is uniform: Spanish 'abundancia/saciedad,' Arabic 'al-shiba/shiban,' Hindi 'bahutayat/tripti,' Korean 'pungyo/baebuleum/pungseongham,' Swahili 'wingi/kushiba/zitajaa tele.' No semantic distinction exists between the clusters.
